summary: Monday's post-market layer puts the composite at its highest level of this sample: the risk score rose 2.7 to 48.38 with the regime unchanged at goldilocks, and it did so against a broadly lower US tape. 20 of the 22 sector and theme rows closed lower, led by autos at -3.9272 and autonomous driving at -3.2052, with AI software -2.5779, data centers -2.5152 and AI infrastructure -2.4821 all in the weakest quartile; the only rows higher were cybersecurity at 0.9163 and gaming at 0.3011. Nvidia was the single large-cap holdout, adding 1.8402 to 229.211807, and it is the one name in the tracked complex that the day's news flow explains rather than contradicts. What lifted the score was not the tape but the alignment of the risk blocks: cross-asset confirmation jumped to 0.75 from 0.625, taking triggered signals to 7 of 10, and the macro block stayed binding at 67.8 with the 10-year real rate at 2.85 from 2.76 and the nominal 10-year at 5.18 from 5.11, both at the 100.0th percentile of their own histories. Volatility is the mirror image: VIX fell to 14.21 from 14.87 and sits in the 15.56th percentile, so the model is scoring structural and rate-linked stress rather than fear. Breadth stayed thin, with 1 new high against 18 new lows across 155 names and just 0.5677 of them above their 200-day average. Two caveats belong in the text rather than in the data. The newest FRED rate vintage is dated 2026-09-24, so the rate block describes the end of last week rather than today's press accounts of yields pressing to multiyear highs. And this layer's tracked mainland names still carry the 2026-09-24 close, so the A-share session is taken from the earlier Dublin snapshot, in which all 11 names closed lower.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Cross-asset confirmation jumped to 0.75 from 0.625, taking triggered signals to 7 of 10 and making this the largest single contributor to the composite at 7.5. Copper turned negative and gold flipped lower as well, so the non-equity complex is no longer offsetting the equity signal.

The macro block remains the binding constraint at 67.8: the 10-year real rate rose to 2.85 from 2.76 and the nominal 10-year to 5.18 from 5.11, both at the 100.0th percentile of their own histories. Policy pricing still leans to a hike, with the implied rate at 4.205 against an effective 3.88.

The US tape closed broadly lower: 20 of the 22 sector and theme rows fell, with autos at -3.9272 the weakest and autonomous driving at -3.2052 close behind, while AI software -2.5779, fintech -2.5218 and data centers -2.5152 each lost more than 2.5.

Liquidity tightened at the margin: the reverse repo facility fell to 0.851 from 0.576, which puts it in the 6.9th percentile and drives an 86.2 risk reading on that single input, while reserve balances dropped to 2930193 from 3013794 and the Treasury General Account rose to 977084 from 877028.

Credit widened again: HY OAS moved to 2.93 from 2.8 and IG OAS to 0.81 from 0.79, contributing 3.4144 to the composite, even though both remain far from the levels that would trigger the spread signal.

supporting_signals.claim: Breadth kept thinning: only 1 of 155 names printed a new high against 18 new lows, and just 0.5677 of the sample sits above its 200-day average, with semis relative at -12.0296 and small caps at -9.5864.

The tracked A-share AI panel closed all 11 names lower, from -2.7506 to -7.6184, a deeper drawdown than the US complex managed. That reading is taken from the earlier Dublin snapshot rather than from this layer's index, which still carries the 2026-09-24 close.
Crypto added to the risk-off signal: bitcoin fell to 83514, down 1.37679, which triggered the bitcoin-down cross-asset signal, with solana weaker still at -3.4402.
The dollar index held at 119.5133, keeping the dollar-strength signal triggered and capping the case for a broad risk-on rotation.

The trend block is the lowest-scoring of the six at 44.83 with the 52-week drawdown at -1.5324, and the composite's own consistency factor fell to 0.6819 while data quality stayed at 1.0 - the model is holding a high score on inputs that disagree with one another.

contradicting_signals.claim: Volatility priced calm: VIX fell to 14.21 from 14.87 and sits in the 15.56th percentile, with realized volatility at 11.0558 and the volatility block at 14.93 by far the lowest of the six.

Nvidia was the single large-cap holdout, adding 1.8402 to 229.211807 after the company announced the largest share-repurchase authorization increase in history, so the AI complex did not crack uniformly.
Credit did not confirm: HY OAS at 2.93 is still far below the 4 level that would trigger the widening signal, and the cross-asset count stayed at 7 of 10 rather than aligning fully.
The regime held at goldilocks with 3-month momentum still positive at 3.3684 and the index 6.5511 above its 200-day average, so the model sees an intact uptrend.

The layer's most acute inputs are vintage-stale: the rate block is dated 2026-09-24 and the tracked mainland names still carry the 2026-09-24 close, so part of the day's calm reading is an artefact of data timing rather than a market that is genuinely calm.

what_changed_today: The composite rose 2.7 to 48.38, its highest reading of the sample, while the regime stayed at goldilocks.
Cross-asset confirmation moved to 0.75 from 0.625, lifting triggered signals to 7 of 10.
The rate vintage advanced to 2026-09-24: the 10-year moved to 5.18 from 5.11, the 2-year to 4.87 from 4.85 and the real rate to 2.85 from 2.76.
Liquidity shifted: the reverse repo facility fell to 0.851 from 0.576 while reserve balances fell to 2930193 from 3013794 and the Treasury General Account rose to 977084 from 877028.
Credit widened modestly: HY OAS to 2.93 from 2.8 and IG OAS to 0.81 from 0.79.
Volatility fell away from the tape: VIX to 14.21 from 14.87, even as 20 of the 22 sector and theme rows closed lower.
The tracked A-share panel closed all 11 names lower, from -2.7506 to -7.6184, taken from the earlier Dublin snapshot rather than this layer's index.
watch_next: Whether the composite holds its 48.38 reading or mean-reverts, given that the trend block at 44.83 and a consistency factor of 0.6819 are the weakest parts of the picture.
The calendar lists a high-importance FOMC meeting on 2026-09-28T18:00Z with no outcome recorded in this layer; the implied policy rate at 4.205 still sits above the effective 3.88.

Tomorrow's data run and the week's high-importance releases: job openings and CCL earnings on 2026-09-29, then personal income and outlays and GDP on 2026-09-30, ahead of the employment situation on 2026-10-02.
Whether credit or volatility finally confirm the tape: HY OAS 2.93, IG OAS 0.81 and VIX 14.21 all still price calm.
Whether the tracked mainland panel's all-lower session transmits into US hardware, or stays an Asia-local de-rating that the US tape has so far priced only partially.
Whether the rate data catches up to the press account of yields pressing to multiyear highs, since the layer's newest observation is still dated 2026-09-24.

bull_case.title: Volatility and credit hold the line
points: Credit and volatility keep pricing calm (HY OAS 2.93, IG OAS 0.81, VIX 14.21) while Nvidia's buyback-backed strength at 229.211807 offsets the AI-complex de-rating.
The real rate mean-reverts from 2.85 and the 10-year from 5.18 without any policy move, unwinding the binding constraint on its own.
An energy-premium unwind after the Saudi pipeline restart drains the inflation impulse and lets the front end lead a curve rally.

base_case.title: High score, quiet tape, no break
points: The composite holds near 48.38 while the macro block pins the real rate near 2.85 and the 10-year near 5.18.
The US and mainland sessions keep running independently, with the mainland panel's decline failing to transmit into US hardware.
Volatility stays near 14.21 into the FOMC and the week's data run, leaving the score high but the tape unbroken.

bear_case.title: The long end and the AI complex break together
points: The 10-year extends beyond 5.18 and the real rate beyond 2.85 while the narrow leadership (semis relative -12.0296, small caps -9.5864) rolls over.
Credit follows: HY OAS moves up from 2.93 toward the widening trigger and the corporate-spread signal flips out of dormancy.
The AI-adjacent themes accelerate lower (AI software -2.5779, data centers -2.5152, AI infrastructure -2.4821) and drag out the sample's single new high.
